title: Home strip says '(server busy)' on an idle, offline server, beside 'Automatic collection: stopped'
repro: Boot and unlock. Stay offline and do nothing that writes, and stay on Home for about 90 s. Then read the at-a-glance strip (#home-stats).
expected: The note should appear only when the counts are really being held back by a busy server, or it should state their real age without giving a cause. On an idle server nothing was written and the counts are current.
actual: Once the cached payload is 90 s old, the strip ends with 'as of 06:23 AM (server busy)', and the same note appears in fr ('serveur occupé'), ar and zh. The status line beside it says 'Automatic collection: stopped'. At the same time the API reports scheduler running:false and online:false, and /api/database/stats shows cache_age_s growing 89→209 with an unchanged as_of. An operator in airplane mode is told the server is busy when nothing is running.
recheck_evidence: Own instance: a fresh encrypted mini seed at /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/H-recheck/data-enc (ui_clickthrough_seed.py --mini with OO_DB_PASSPHRASE set; the DB header is ciphertext), booted on 8950 with neither variable set. lock-state read 'locked'; I unlocked through #pw/#btn-unlock and stayed on Home doing nothing. My probe (rc_busy.py) sent no stats requests of its own and only recorded Home's own /api/database/stats polls. as_of stayed 09:06:10 while cache_age_s rose 14 -> 119. At dt=150 s the strip ended 'as of 09:06 AM (server busy)' while #home-status said 'Automatic collection: stopped'. At that moment /api/scheduler/status read running:false, active:false, online:false, and its own server_load read loop_lag 0.3 ms, heavy in_flight 0/4, busy_refusals 0, memory_guard engaged:false. /api/system/network read online:false. After live switches: fr 'à 09:06 (serveur occupé)', ar '(الخادم مشغول)', zh '（服务器繁忙）'. Files: /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/H-recheck/rc_busy.json and shots/rc-home-busy-en-strip.png, rc-home-busy-{en,fr,ar,zh}.png. No page, console or HTTP errors. This is not a harness artifact.
root_cause: src/static/app-home.js:117-137. homeStatsAgeNote() tests only payload.cache_age_s >= 90 and always names the cause as '(server busy)'. But src/api/served_cache.py:233-245 is written to keep built_at when the grants probe shows nothing was written: it re-stamps only checked_at, and as_of/cache_age_s are derived from built_at (served_cache.py:152). So on an idle server the value is verified as exactly right, yet cache_age_s grows without limit, and the note fires because the server is idle. The S3.4(d) brief (docs/design/AUTONOMOUS_SESSION_BRIEF_2026-09-02_CRASH_ROOT_CAUSE.md:825) ties the note to a stale-served payload. No ruling covers the idle case: grep of OPEN_QUEUE/RULINGS_INDEX/LESSONS found nothing, and planned.py reports nothing for app-home.js.
suggested_fix: In served_cache._decorate, also publish the age since the value was last verified or rebuilt (now - checked_at), or a verified_unchanged flag. Show '(server busy)' only when that verification age is >= 90 s, which means a rebuild is pending or in flight. For a value that was verified unchanged, show nothing, or a cause-free 'unchanged since HH:MM'. Alternatively, gate the cause on /api/scheduler/status server_load. Add a node test for the idle case: cache_age_s 120 with a fresh verification gives no 'server busy'.

title: External topic discovery: the Enabled/Disabled disclosure line and both toasts are English in every non-English locale
repro: Switch the top bar to Français (or العربية), then open Settings > Advanced > 'Safety & at-risk use' and tick 'Autoriser les requêtes de découverte de sujets vers DuckDuckGo'. Untick it again.
expected: The line that discloses the egress ('… queries will be sent to DuckDuckGo') and the toasts are in the UI language. Every consent or caveat string ships in all 12 locales (the informed-consent non-negotiable), like the checkbox label beside it.
actual: In fr and ar the line reads 'Enabled: topic-discovery queries will be sent to DuckDuckGo.' then 'Disabled (the default): no topic query leaves this machine.', and the toasts read 'External topic discovery enabled.' / 'External topic discovery disabled.'. All are English. The English line also stays on screen after a later switch to ar.
recheck_evidence: rc_disc.py on my instance, in fr then ar: Settings > Advanced > Safety & at-risk use, tick #discovery-external, then untick. The label beside the box is translated (fr 'Autoriser les requêtes de découverte de sujets vers DuckDuckGo', ar 'السماح بإرسال استعلامات اكتشاف المواضيع إلى DuckDuckGo'), and so is the disclosure paragraph (keyed 12/12). In both locales the result line reads 'Enabled: topic-discovery queries will be sent to DuckDuckGo.' then 'Disabled (the default): no topic query leaves this machine.', and the toasts read 'External topic discovery enabled.' / 'External topic discovery disabled.'. After a live switch to zh the line still reads the English 'Disabled (the default)…'. In zh the page's own lookup returns all four strings unchanged, while 'Fetch mode saved.' gives '抓取模式已保存。'. A locale scan finds 0 of 12 files carrying any of the four keys. The setting was restored to false and network stayed online:false. Files: /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/H-recheck/rc_disc.json, shots/rc-disc-fr-on.png, rc-disc-ar-on.png, rc-disc-zh-after-switch.png.
root_cause: src/static/app-backup.js:3126-3128. saveDiscoveryExternal() writes the two result sentences into #discovery-external-result with textContent and passes the two toast sentences to toast() as bare English literals. None of the four is wrapped in t() or keyed in src/static/locales/*.json. The DOM walker (src/static/i18n.js:34-44) translates only exact keys, so the four stay English, on first paint and after a live switch alike. toast() (src/static/app-core.js:510-512) does not translate.
suggested_fix: Add the four strings to all 12 locale files. Pass the toasts through OOI18N.t. For the result line, either write the English key and let the walker translate it on paint and on oo:langchange, or render with t() on an element marked data-i18n-dyn and repaint it on oo:langchange. Do not write a translated string into a walker-owned node, or it gets cached as the English original. Extend the i18n chrome audit so it catches textContent/toast literals like these.

title: Help 'Find on this page…': typing a phrase whose first match is in the Security endpoint table highlights it but does not scroll it into view
repro: Open Help (top-bar ?) > Security. Click 'Find on this page…' and TYPE 'Where in the tree' key by key (as H4 says). Tried at 20, 60, 80 and 200 ms per key, and with a final Enter.
expected: The page jumps to the highlighted match (the table header), as it does when the same text is pasted.
actual: The match is highlighted (1 mark) and the wide table scrolls sideways (scrollLeft 519 at 1440, 962 at 375), but the page does not scroll down. The mark stays at y≈1790-1836 in a 950 px viewport, with page scrollY ≈111-159, 3-4 s later. A single fill/paste of the same text does jump (scrollY 1479, mark at y=468). Typed phrases whose match is in plain prose ('kept true', 'Reporting') also jump.
recheck_evidence: rc_find.py: each case ran on a fresh page, with Help > Security opened and scrollY set to 0. Typed 'Where in the tree' at 60 ms per key: 1 mark, table scrollLeft 519, page scrollY 125, mark top 1822 in a 950 px viewport (out of view). At 200 ms per key: scrollY 163, mark top 1784. Typed plus Enter, then 8 s: scrollY 125. At 375x667: scrollY 210, mark top 5025, table scrollLeft 962. fill() gives scrollY 1479, mark top 468 (1440), and scrollY 4908, mark top 327 (375). keyboard.insert_text also gives scrollY 1479. Typed prose 'kept true' does jump (scrollY 503, mark top 466). Controls: forcing behavior:'auto' on scrollIntoView still fails (scrollY 111 at 1440, 161 at 375, with the window pulled back in the same frame as each input event). Deferring the unchanged smooth call with setTimeout(0) lands (scrollY 1479, mark top 468). rc_find_ctl.py: after typing, #doc-find sits at top -30 / bottom 14, just brought back into the viewport, the signature of the caret reveal that follows a keystroke. Files: /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/H-recheck/rc_find.json, rc_find_ctl.json, shots/rc-find-typed60-1440.png, rc-find-filled-1440.png, rc-find-typed60-375.png, rc-find-typed60-DEFER0-1440.png. Playwright's keyboard.type goes through the same editing path as a real keypress, so this is not a harness artifact.
root_cause: src/static/app-settings.js:85. highlightProse() calls first.scrollIntoView({block:'center', behavior:'smooth'}) synchronously inside the #doc-find input handler (src/static/index.html:3210 oninput="filterDoc()" -> app-settings.js:66-70). After a real keystroke's input event returns, Chromium reveals the focused input's caret. That reveal overrides or aborts the page-level part of the scroll. When the match sits inside the horizontally scrollable table, the scroll is a two-step sequence (table, then page), and only the table step survives. A paste or fill makes no keystroke caret reveal, and a prose match needs only the page step, which is already animating, so both work.
suggested_fix: Move the scroll out of the input event. A setTimeout(0) or requestAnimationFrame is enough (measured). Better, debounce filterDoc by about 150 ms, which also stops re-rendering the whole Help body on every keystroke. Optionally, scroll the table wrapper and the page as two explicit steps.

title: Result block 'Already judged here, kept' over-counts: per-item snapshots are summed across a multi-backup run
repro:
1. On tgtB, after importing the 4 distinct backups (a corpus with about 6 446 sources), open Settings → Data & backup → Import.
2. Scan /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/I/backups_cum (4 cumulative backups).
3. Import only the corpus, with the dialog kept open until the result block renders.
4. Look at the source-qualification part of the result block.
expected: 'Already judged here, kept' counts each source at most once. It can never exceed the number of sources in the corpus.
actual: 'Already judged here, kept: 19 254' (ar «سبق الحكم عليها هنا، أُبقيت: 19 254», zh «此处已判定并保留：19 254»). That is about three times the corpus's 6 446 sources. The per-item plans' _source_qualification.local_verdict_kept values are 6400, 6422, 6418 and 14, and the UI adds them up.
recheck_evidence:
My own instance: /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/I-recheck/tgt1 on port 8953. Created through the real first launch (en, legal, the data-location step, passphrase walk-pass-2026). It booted with lock-state 'locked' and was unlocked through #pw/#btn-unlock. I imported copies of the walker's backup sets (copied into /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/I-recheck/backups and /backups_cum): first the 4 distinct backups in fr, then the 4 cumulative backups in zh with the dialog open.

Source counts, paged through /api/sources/: 6 416 before the cumulative import and 6 446 after it.

The zh result block reads '此处已判定并保留：19 254'. See events.jsonl R_zh_result_block and shots/zh-result-block.png.

The persisted per-item reports rep-5..8.json (plan._source_qualification.local_verdict_kept) give 6400, 6422, 6418 and 14. Their sum is exactly 19 254, three times the corpus's 6 446 sources.
root_cause: src/static/app-backup.js:2627 does `qualKept += pq.local_verdict_kept || 0` for every counted item, and :2771 renders the sum as 'Already judged here, kept'. Each item's figure (src/backup/merge.py:2188, `local_verdict_kept`) counts every incoming source that already had a local verdict. A source carried by N backups of the same run is therefore counted N times. The other qualification counters (introduced/adopted) are disjoint across items and sum correctly; this one does not.
suggested_fix: Give the aggregate a distinct count. Either the queue computes a run-level tally of the distinct local source ids whose verdict was kept (union across the run's items), or the aggregate drops this line for multi-item runs and leaves the figure in each backup's own detail. Do not sum per-item snapshots. The first walk's I6 (a re-index backlog summed per item) had the same shape and was rated P2, hence P2 here.

title: Raw backend sentinel 'unrecorded' shown as an engine name in 'Judged by'

root_cause: src/backup/merge.py:2166-2170 deliberately reports a verdict with no recorded criteria version under the literal key 'unrecorded' (docstring :2152-2155). src/static/app-backup.js:2773-2777 then joins `${e} (${num(n)})` for every engine key without mapping that sentinel to a translated phrase.
suggested_fix: In the Judged-by join, map the key 'unrecorded' to t('engine not recorded'), keyed x12, and leave real criteria versions (v1 ...) as data. Alternatively the backend can send the sentinel as null/None with a separate count, and the UI words it.

title: Reopening Import after a scan keeps the previous scan's trust row, its caveat and the folder path
repro:
1. Open Import and scan /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/I/backups.
2. Close the dialog without running.
3. Reopen Import.
expected: The dialog reopens clean: no trust row and no leftover folder, or all of the scan's parts kept together.
actual: The checklist, status and passphrase row are cleared and Run is disabled, but #ux-imp-trust-row stays visible (display:block) with its caveat. The old folder path also stays in #ux-imp-src. The result is a half-reset form showing a trust statement for a scan that is no longer shown. This is an R1 residue.
recheck_evidence: en. I scanned /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/I-recheck/backups, closed the dialog without running, and reopened it. Measured 1.5 s and 5.5 s after the reopen: trust row display 'block' with its caveat, #ux-imp-src still holding the path, checklist '', status '', pass-row 'none', Run disabled (events.jsonl I5_reopen_1_5s / I5_reopen_5_5s, shots/i5-reopen-dialog-en.png). A trust checkbox and its caveat stand under an empty checklist. It is worse after a FINISHED import: reopening after the fr and zh runs also showed the trust row as 'block' (I5b_reopen_after_import, R_zh_reopen_row4.st). S04-02 S2's acceptance for a reopen is 'the line, nothing else'.
root_cause: src/static/app-backup.js:923-946 (openUnifiedImport) resets the checklist, status, progress, summary, last line, bar, pass-row and Run, and calls _uxImResetRunView (:2199), but never hides #ux-imp-trust-row. That row's display is set only by _uxImTrustRow (:1196-1199), which only a scan calls. #ux-imp-src is not cleared either.
suggested_fix: In openUnifiedImport, call the trust-row hide as well (row.style.display='none', or _uxImTrustRow(false)). Then decide deliberately whether the folder path should persist. Keeping it as a convenience is defensible, but then the form should not look half-scanned.

title: Stage 4's dot stays grey ('not started' colour) while the re-index is running
repro: Finish an import with the dialog open, or reopen it while the re-index drains, and look at stage row 4 while it reads 'resuming re-index — X of Y'.
expected: The dot uses the running colour while the job runs and the done colour when the backlog reaches 0.
actual: The dot stays var(--muted), the colour used for 'not started', throughout the run even as the text counts up.
recheck_evidence: fr, dialog kept open after the run. For 12 s, row 4 read 'reprise de la réindexation — 200 … 1 000 articles sur 4 800' while /reindex-backlog/resume/status was 'running'. The dot was var(--muted) = rgb(92,101,115) at every sample (events I7_fr_open_seq, shots/i7-fr-open-stages-crop.png). It was the same on reopens mid-drain (I7_fr_reopen, I7_fr_drain_reopen at 2 100 and 3 600 of 4 800) and in zh (R_zh_reopen_row4). Once finished, row 4 reads 'complete' and the dot is still var(--muted) (I4_ar_gap/I4_en_gap reindex bg var(--muted)), so neither the running colour nor the done colour ever appears.
root_cause: src/backup/import_queue.py:1307 always reports the reindex stage as state 'external', by design, because the queue does not own that job. src/static/app-backup.js:1892-1895 colours every stage row's dot from sRow.state alone, so 'external' maps to var(--muted) while the row's TEXT comes from rx (_uxImReindexBits). Text and dot are fed by different sources.
suggested_fix: For key==='reindex', derive the dot from rx, the same status the text uses: running gives var(--accent); a zero backlog with nothing left gives var(--ok); idle with a backlog gives var(--warn); unread stays var(--muted).

title: A page reload during an export's corpus phase silently drops the large-data copy the user ticked; the reopened dialog still reads 'Backup complete' and 'Verified'
repro:
1. Encrypted install whose LLM models store holds files (here HF_HOME=/tmp/claude-0/rewalk/J/fake-hf, shown as 'LLM models (3 files · 2.9 MB)', ticked by default).
2. Settings → Data & backup → Export / Back up…
3. Destination /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/J/exports-reload-models and a passphrase. Leave LLM models ticked and 'Carry them inside the encrypted backup' unticked. Click 'Back up'.
4. As soon as #ux-progress reads 'Corpus: Preparing…', reload the page (F5).
5. Wait for /api/backup/v2/volumes/status to reach done, then reopen the dialog and list the folder.
expected: The large-data copy the user asked for still runs to completion server-side, or the reopened dialog says this export is INCOMPLETE: the LLM models were requested and not copied, with a way to finish. The app's own comment (app-backup.js, _uxShowLastCompletedExportSummary) says a long export's tab is very likely closed or reloaded before it finishes, so this is the realistic case, not an edge.
actual:
202609270849_OpenOmniscience_Backup holds only volumes.json, par-00001.oopar, 4 .ooenc and BACKUP_SUMMARY.md. It has no hf_models/ and no oo-folder-backup.json. /api/backup/folder/status still names the OLDER drive/202609270847 export: the copy was never started. /api/jobs lists nothing.

The reopened dialog reads 'Backup complete → …/202609270849_OpenOmniscience_Backup (last completed export)', then a clean 'Verified — all 4 volumes were re-read and matched their checksums.' and 'Files copied: no files'. There is no 'Included:' line, no Resume, and nothing that says LLM models were asked for. BACKUP_SUMMARY.md says 'Files copied: none.' The corpus is intact; the requested member is missing with no signal.
recheck_evidence:
Reproduced on my own instance: a fresh encrypted seed at /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/J-recheck/data-enc, nothing copied. Port 8956 started locked and I unlocked it through #pw/#btn-unlock. I used my own synthetic HF_HOME store (3 files, 2.9 MB) and stayed in airplane mode throughout.

CONTROL, no reload (results/control-1440x950.json). With Corpus and LLM models ticked and inside unticked, the progress ran 'Corpus: … → Large data: … → Backup complete → …/drive/202609271124_OpenOmniscience_Backup' and then 'Included: Corpus · LLM models'. That folder holds hf_models/ and oo-folder-backup.json, and the panel says 'Files copied: hf_models 3 files · 2.9 MB'.

RELOAD (results/reload-1440x950.json). pre_reload.at_click shows ux-c-models checked and ux-c-inside unchecked. I reloaded as soon as the progress read 'Corpus: Preparing…'. Afterwards the volumes status reported done for exports-reload-models/202609271124_OpenOmniscience_Backup. After another 8 s, /api/backup/folder/status still named the OLDER drive/202609271124_OpenOmniscience_Backup (started_at 1790501078.68, before this export's 1790501098.80). /api/jobs was empty. server.log shows export-folder and volumes/start for this export and NO POST /api/backup/folder/start after them.

The folder lists only BACKUP_SUMMARY.md, par-00001.oopar, 4 .ooenc and volumes.json: no hf_models/ and no oo-folder-backup.json. BACKUP_SUMMARY.md says 'Files copied: none.'

The reopened dialog shows 'Backup complete → …/202609271124_OpenOmniscience_Backup (last completed export)', then 'Verified — all 4 volumes…' and 'Files copied: no files'. It has no 'Included:' line and no Resume (the #ux-pause display is none). The checklist still shows LLM models ticked. Screenshots: shots/reload-models-reopen-en.png and reload-models-reopen-bottom-en.png. No page errors, console errors or HTTP >= 400.

This is not a harness artifact: the reload was a plain page.reload() at a moment any user can hit. No ruling or manual text tells the user to keep the tab open, and the app's own comment at app-backup.js:71-80 says a reload is the likely case.
root_cause:
src/static/app-backup.js:807-813. The browser's _uxRun closure is the only thing that starts the large-data phase (POST /api/backup/folder/start), and only after it has polled the corpus phase to done (:784-805). A reload destroys that closure, so the copy never starts.

The server never learns the copy was requested. POST /api/backup/export-folder (src/api/backup_v2.py:592-613) records only the parent folder. /v2/volumes/start gets include_blobs only in the 'inside' case (app-backup.js:786-788; VolumeBackupBody at backup_v2.py:455-466).

On reopen, _uxShowLastCompletedExportSummary (app-backup.js:81-148, the line at :122) treats the volume job's done as a completed export. _uxExportIncluded (:835) died with the page and nothing server-side holds the request, so no 'Included:' line and no incomplete state can be drawn. export_facts can only describe what is on disk.
suggested_fix:
Make the export one server-side job, the way the import queue was after ruling item 16. Pass the requested members (corpus, categories, inside) with the folder allocation or with /v2/volumes/start, and have the volume manager start the folder copy into the same dest when the corpus phase completes.

At minimum, persist the request inside the dated folder (for example oo-export-request.json, written at allocation). The reopened dialog and export_facts can then compare requested with present and show 'Incomplete: LLM models were requested and not copied', with a button that starts /api/backup/folder/start into the same dest. BACKUP_SUMMARY.md should name the missing member too, instead of 'Files copied: none.'

title: Consent popup lane list can still read '…' seconds after opening while 'Go online' is already enabled (intermittent)

title: Home strip says 'as of 08:20 AM (server busy)' on an idle, offline app whose counts are current
repro: Folder B, 1440x950, en. Unlock, stay in airplane mode with nothing running (scheduler running:false), wait about 2 minutes after the first stats read, then open Home (or switch language on Home).
expected: No 'server busy' claim while the server is idle. An age note should appear only when the numbers may really be stale, for example when writes happened since the cached build or a rebuild is pending, and its wording should say what is actually known.
actual: The strip adds 'as of 08:20 AM (server busy)' (fr 'à 08:20 (serveur occupé)'). At that moment /api/database/stats returned cached:true, cache_age_s 471, and /api/scheduler/status running:false with network offline. The server is idle and nothing was written, so the counts are exact, yet the strip tells the reader the server is busy and implies the figures are stale.
recheck_evidence: My own instance, en, 1440x950, idle and offline: scheduler running:false and /api/system/network online:false throughout. At 10:13:00 /api/database/stats returned as_of 10:11:59, cache_age_s 60, and the strip showed no note. By 10:13:49 cache_age_s was 109, and after a live switch to fr and back and after a reload the strip read 'as of 10:11 AM (server busy)'. fr reads 'à 10:11 (serveur occupé)' and ar reads 'حتى 10:11 ص (الخادم مشغول)'. Four curl samples 20 s apart (10:14:15 to 10:15:15) returned the same built_at 10:11:59, with age going 135 → 155 → 175 → 195 against cache_ttl_s 30. By served_cache.cached, an entry past its TTL keeps its built_at only when the write-gate probe is unchanged, so the server itself had verified that nothing was written and the counts were exact. The server log has no 'served-cache background refresh failed'. The same /api/scheduler/status reported server_load loop_lag latest_ms 0.0, heavy in_flight 0 and memory_guard engaged:false, so the server was demonstrably not busy. Shots: /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/P-recheck/shots/Prc-home-0-en.png (no note at age 60), Prc-home-idle-age-note-en.png, Prc-home-idle-age-note-en-reload.png, Prc-home-idle-age-note-fr.png. Data: rc_main.json (stats0, stats_samples, home_strip_*), stats_idle_samples.txt. This is not by-design. Brief S3.4(d) (docs/design/AUTONOMOUS_SESSION_BRIEF_2026-09-02_CRASH_ROOT_CAUSE.md:825) asks for the note on a STALE-served payload. served_cache.py:233-240 itself says an idle, probe-verified entry 'is not merely fresh enough -- it is still exactly right'. Audit 11 (:473) praised the note as appearing 'only when the stats cache is genuinely stale', which this contradicts.
root_cause: src/static/app-home.js:117-137. homeStatsAgeNote decides on cache_age_s >= 90 alone and always appends '(server busy)'. src/api/served_cache.py:236-245 re-stamps checked_at but deliberately keeps built_at on an idle, probe-verified serve. _decorate (served_cache.py:139-153) exposes only as_of, cache_age_s and cached, never whether the value was verified unchanged or is waiting on a recount. So on every idle install the note fires 90 s after the first build and stays.
suggested_fix: In served_cache.cached, add a field to the decorated payload: `verified_current: probe is not None and probe == snapshot['probe']`, or `refresh_pending: True` when _kick_background_refresh ran. In homeStatsAgeNote, show the note only when the payload is not verified current, and word it by what is known ('as of {time} · recount pending') rather than asserting 'server busy'. Alternatively, add '(server busy)' only when /api/scheduler/status server_load shows heavy.in_flight > 0 or loop lag. Add a node test: an idle payload with age 400 and verified_current:true renders no note.

title: Home's at-a-glance strip says 'as of HH:MM (server busy)' on an idle server
repro: Boot normally (airplane mode, collection stopped). Unlock and stay on Home, or reload it more than 90 s after the counts were last built, with nothing running.
expected: No 'server busy' claim when the server is idle. At most an age stamp, or wording that does not give a false reason.
actual: 'as of 08:39 AM (server busy)' / 'à 08:39 (serveur occupé)' / '(الخادم مشغول)' / '（服务器繁忙）' while the scheduler is stopped and the app is in airplane mode. /api/database/stats as_of stays fixed while cache_age_s grows (46 then 66 over 20 idle seconds).
recheck_evidence:
rc_busy.json:
- After unlock the app stays on Home with nothing running: /api/scheduler/status running:false, /api/scheduler/activity {running:false, active:false, phase:null, online:false}, airplane mode.
- /api/database/stats as_of stays '2026-09-27T10:25:16+00:00' while cache_age_s grows 18, 36, 54, 72, 90, 96 across 18 s samples, with cached:true and cache_ttl_s 30.
- After a reload at age 96 s the strip reads '… 10 MENTIONED DATES as of 10:25 AM (server busy)'. In fr it reads 'à 10:25 (serveur occupé)', in ar 'حتى 10:25 ص (الخادم مشغول)', in zh '截至 10:25（服务器繁忙）'.
- Screenshot: /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/T-recheck/shots/busy-home-en-reload.png. 'Automatic collection: stopped' sits two lines under '(server busy)'.
- The cache's own comment says the idle value 'is still exactly right'.
- Severity P2 rather than P3: the stamp states a false reason about the system's state on the app's default path (offline, idle, more than 90 s after the last write).
root_cause: src/static/app-home.js:113-138. `homeStatsAgeNote` appends t("as of {time} (server busy)") whenever `cache_age_s >= 90` (:117, :120, :137). src/api/served_cache.py:235-244 deliberately leaves `built_at`, and therefore `as_of` and `cache_age_s` (:146-152), untouched when the change probe shows no write, i.e. on an idle server. It only re-stamps `checked_at`, which the payload never exposes. So on an idle server the age grows without bound and the note fires with a reason nothing measured.
suggested_fix: Expose the verification in the payload. `_decorate` can add `verified_age_s` (now − checked_at) or `refresh_pending: bool` (true when the probe differed and a background rebuild was kicked). The Home note should key on that: show nothing when the value was verified unchanged, and only when a rebuild is pending say 'as of {time} (refreshing)'. Never give 'server busy' as a reason unless it is measured. Keep the 90 s threshold for the pending case.

title: Home strip says '(server busy)' on an idle app, beside counts the server has just re-verified as exact
repro: Unlock any corpus, leave the app idle for more than 90 s (no collection, no jobs, airplane mode), then open Home and read the at-a-glance strip, in any language.
expected: No 'server busy' claim while nothing is running. The counts are exact (nothing was written), so at most an honest 'as of' with no busy claim.
actual: The strip reads 'as of 09:07 AM (server busy)' (fr 'à 09:07 (serveur occupé)', ar 'حتى 09:07 ص (الخادم مشغول)') for as long as the app stays idle. At that moment /api/scheduler/activity running:false, /api/jobs is empty, and /api/database/stats returns cache_age_s 318 with ttl 30, cached true. The age grows without bound on an idle app, so the busy note becomes permanent on every idle install.
recheck_evidence: My own encrypted STATE C seed in /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/U-recheck/seeded. Booted on port 8980 with neither OO_DB_* variable set. lock-state read locked; I unlocked through #pw/#btn-unlock and it then read unlocked-encrypted. I stayed on Home and touched nothing. I sampled /api/database/stats every 20 s (walk_a.json strip.samples). as_of stayed at 10:30:19 from t=44 s to t=144 s while cache_age_s rose 13→33→53→73→93→113, with cached true and ttl 30. Articles stayed at 453. At t=144 s the strip read 'as of 10:30 AM (server busy)'. After a live switch, fr read 'à 10:30 (serveur occupé)' and ar read 'حتى 10:30 ص (الخادم مشغول)'. At the same moment /api/scheduler/activity returned running:false and /api/jobs returned []. Shots: /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/U-recheck/shots/A1-strip-busy-en-crop.png, A1-strip-busy-fr-crop.png, A1-strip-busy-ar-crop.png. This is not by design. Brief S3.4(d) (docs/design/AUTONOMOUS_SESSION_BRIEF_2026-09-02_CRASH_ROOT_CAUSE.md:825) asks for the note on a STALE-SERVED payload. served_cache.py:236-244 says a value the probe verifies as unchanged 'is still exactly right'. The note therefore claims load exactly when there is none.
root_cause: src/static/app-home.js:117-120 (homeStatsAgeNote) shows the busy note whenever payload.cache_age_s >= 90. cache_age_s is time since BUILD (src/api/served_cache.py:152, _decorate). On an idle app, served_cache.cached() at :236-244 only re-stamps checked_at and deliberately never rebuilds, so built_at never moves and the age grows without bound. The payload carries no field that separates 'verified unchanged' from 'stale while a rebuild is pending', so the client reads every verified idle value as a busy server.
suggested_fix: In served_cache._decorate, also expose the verification state. Either add checked_age_s from entry['checked_at'], or add a 'stale' flag that is true only when the probe differs or a background refresh was kicked. In homeStatsAgeNote, show '(server busy)' only when that flag says the value is stale (or checked_age_s >= 90). When the value is verified unchanged, show nothing, or a neutral 'as of HH:MM' with no busy claim. Add a node or pytest check: an idle cache older than 90 s yields no busy note.
